nodes.notes: 1) Class: fused Conv2D(3x3,s=1,pad=1) + bias + ReLU + AvgPool2x2, fp16. Dense, no reduction outside conv (sum over C_in*Kh*Kw=144). 2) Output Y[b,oc,oh,ow] = ReLU(sum_ic,kh,kw X[b,ic,oh*2+kh-1+dh, ow*2+kw-1+dw] * W[oc,ic,kh,kw] + bias[oc]) then averaged over 2x2 -> output spatial 360x640. Equivalent: each output covers 4 conv outputs over 2x2; pool average with 4 conv outputs which themselves share input footprint of 4x4 region. 3) Layout NCHW fp16 contiguous; weights 32x16x3x3 tiny (9KB) -> fits in shared/registers easily. Bias 32 fp16. 4) Regimes: (a) BW-bound large image -> fuse all ops, single read of input, single write of pooled output; (b) compute-bound if naive without reuse; (c) edge/padding overhead small. 5) Knobs: tile (BLOCK_OH, BLOCK_OW, BLOCK_OC), keep all OC in registers since OC=32, vectorize along W, preload 4x4 input per output pixel, fuse ReLU+pool. 6) Skeleton: per-program compute tile of pooled outputs; load required input region (BLOCK_OH*2+2)x(BLOCK_OW*2+2) for all C_in=16; load weights into registers/SRAM; for each oc accumulate 4 conv results then ReLU, sum, /4. 7) Families: F1 single fused kernel mapping program->(oc_block, output tile); F2 use torch conv + custom fused bias+relu+avgpool; F3 implicit GEMM via tensor cores.

action.description: Implement a single Triton kernel that, per program, computes a tile of pooled outputs for all 32 output channels: load a (2*BH+2)x(2*BW+2) input patch for all 16 input channels, hold 32x16x3x3 weights (small) and bias in registers/constants, perform 3x3 conv with bias, ReLU, then 2x2 average pool, and write to output. fp16 compute with fp32 accumulators.
action.rationale: Fuses conv+bias+relu+avgpool, eliminating intermediate 32x720x1280 fp16 tensor (~56MB). Single read of input, single write of pooled output -> max BW efficiency. C_in=16 and C_out=32 are tiny so weights fit easily.

kernel_summary: Fused 3x3 stride-1 conv (Cin=16, Cout=32, padding=1, zeros) with bias, ReLU activation, and 2x2 average pool on a 1x16x720x1280 fp16 NCHW tensor on RTX5090. Output shape 1x32x360x640 fp16. Quantization disabled. Tiny weight tensor (32x16x3x3 ~9KB) fits in registers/SMEM. The op is memory-bandwidth dominated: naive eager pipeline materializes a 32x720x1280 fp16 intermediate (~56MB) which can be eliminated by fusing all stages into a single Triton kernel that reads the input once and writes the pooled output once.

Does cuDNN conv2d on RTX5090 already approach memory bandwidth limit for this shape?
Can we exploit tl.dot tensor cores for this 3x3 conv given Cout=32 (below typical 64-wide N tile)?
Is bias broadcast best held as a constexpr-loaded vector per program?
How to handle padding efficiently (masked loads vs explicit boundary kernels)?
